about: A-class files adopted with a known difference from the freeze commit, or whose removal was adopted (design doc 10, section 2.1). A difference pins the file's git blob hash, a removal pins "removed": true; each entry says why. The guard lets exactly that through, and any further edit is caught again.

core/checks/camera_view.py.why: design 27 (D89): v1 is gone and nothing in v2 reads this file - the camera-view hints of the frame-probe prompts; the video judge names the cameras itself

ingest/dsfs.py.why: the listing a command already has is handed to the readers (seed): one listing of the bucket per task instead of three per stage worker; no read path changes - prefetch, exists, glob and the reads are as they were (tests/cli test_the_bucket_is_listed_once_per_task)

ingest/mcap_reader.py.why: mcap streamed from TOS (no source cache): _effective_mapping / _scan_mcap / _payload take an optional open_fn, episode numbering delegates to streams.objects.number_episodes, the muxers accept a file-like sink; no algorithm change - streamed rows equal local rows byte for byte (tests/cli test_tos_mcap_is_streamed, test_episode_clips_are_the_readers_mp4_bytes)

ingest/schema.py.why: design 27 (D89): v1 is gone and nothing in v2 reads this file - the column-name constants of v1's Daft DataFrame (no v2 module imports them)

pipeline/verdict.py.why: design 27 (D89): v1 is gone and nothing in v2 reads this file - v1's hard-gate / soft-score verdict; v2 judges by policy over findings (pipeline/policy.py, pipeline/verdicts.py, design 17)

registry/fk.py.why: design 27 (D89): v1 is gone and nothing in v2 reads this file - a forward-kinematics wrapper for a self-collision check that never shipped (nothing imported it)

vlm_call_kinds.py.why: design 27 (D89, D90): only the call kinds v2 sends are named - probe (task_success's one request) and eef_review; v1's endstate, arbitration, caption and llm went with v1

ingest/dataset_profiles/_README.md.why: design 27 (D89): the profile fields are described by what v2 reads; the arbitration and camera_view.py readers went with v1 (documentation only)

core/checks/video_action_sync.py.why: AV-1 / MV-3 (registry 8.1): windowed_lag reads each camera's lag window by window beside the whole-episode reading (max(window_s, window_min_frames) windows, half-window hop, the same trust rules per window), windows_stable is the one steadiness rule the findings, the report and the console share, sync_health counts the episodes the windowed comparison could speak on; sync_verdict's lines are one scale (spread_tol_s 0.3 -> 0.2, kill_lag_min_s 0.5 -> 0.25 either way) and its misaligned_all is asked, not rejected. global_lag's own measurement is unchanged. Benchmark: spikes/mv3/bench (17 datasets, 149 episodes) - no control episode moves, injected offsets 4/4

core/checks/motion_quality.py.why: ACT-1 / ACT-2 (2026-10-14): smoothness is read column by column against each column's own step scale and averaged (one column's unit or representation no longer drags the rest down), switch-like columns (<= 4 distinct values, e.g. a 0/95 gripper) stay out of smoothness and spike, and a quaternion / rot6d / rotation-matrix block in the action is turned into a rotation odometer like the state's. Parity: on the anchor sample set (19 LeRobot subsets, 205 episodes) the healthy subsets move by at most 0.03 in median smoothness, RH20T goes from 5/5 at 0 to a median of 0.57 and its spike scores from 3/5 low to 0/5, HIW-500 (semantics unknown) abstains instead of scoring 0; two all-zero droid200 episodes that scored 1.0 now abstain. F7b: each column's step scale counts only the frames that move (|step| above a tenth of the column's p95, the spike section's duty rule), so stop-and-go teleoperation (RH20T, HABIT) is no longer read as jagged; on the anchor set RH20T goes 0.57 -> 0.78, HABIT 0.14 -> 0.83, healthy subsets rise by 0.03-0.10, no episode is below 0.5 any more. A positive control (sawtooth / white jitter of 0.25x-2x the moving step injected into real so101 and RH20T episodes) bottoms out at 0.67-0.74: the self-normalised ratio cannot reach 0.5 for zero-mean roughness (pure sawtooth r=2, white noise r=sqrt(3)), and never could - ACT-1's low scores were always pauses. F8: velocity_dims (joystick-style velocity commands named by the dataset) stay out of smoothness and spike like switch columns.

ingest/dataset_semantics.py.why: detect_ee_layout_numeric (2026-10-14): without column names, four consecutive columns of unit norm are a quaternion block, the three before it the translation, discrete or bounded-and-still columns the gripper; a plain rpy or joint array returns None so the old rules apply. Parity: layout detection only; no reading changes on named datasets. F8: column names also classify velocities (vx/vy/vyaw/vel/velocity/speed/omega) and hand controls (trigger/squeeze as grippers); a names layout says whether it is informative (a pose block or translation found).

ingest/lerobot_reader.py.why: _apply_preflight (2026-10-14): the numeric layout fingerprint runs when names are missing, the preflight's gripper columns ride into the layout, and the extras are merged instead of overwritten (the layout was being dropped before it reached motion_quality). Parity: datasets with a profile or names are unchanged; RH20T-like datasets now carry a layout. F8: when the preflight has no verdict (mixed layouts such as HIW-500's chassis velocities + two arm poses + hand controls against a joint-angle state), an informative names layout still rides along marked names_only so motion_quality runs block-wise; the layout written here wins the final extras merge. Parity: the anchor rescan (238 episodes, 16 subsets) changed no reading outside HIW-500, which goes from abstaining to 0.81-0.82.
